corrects_prior_source_inference.prior_conclusion: A Stop event SIGALRM raised as _HookTimeout necessarily transfers to the outer cmd_hook _HookTimeout handler, so a timeout during synchronous cognition necessarily skips the later Stop statements.
corrects_prior_source_inference.correction: That transfer is not guaranteed. _HookTimeout subclasses Exception, while nested model/cognition helpers contain broad except Exception handlers. If SIGALRM raises _HookTimeout while execution is inside one of those protected regions, the cancellation exception can match the nested generic handler, be logged as an ordinary cognition/Ollama error, and be converted to None or otherwise suppressed before the outer cmd_hook handler sees it.

source_atoms.observation: _HookTimeout is declared as a subclass of Exception and _hook_alarm raises _HookTimeout().
source_atoms.implication: The hard-deadline signal is catchable by ordinary broad except Exception clauses.

source_atoms.observation: The synchronous Ollama helper catches expected transport/timeouts and then also catches generic Exception, logs the error, and returns None.
source_atoms.implication: An asynchronously raised _HookTimeout can be consumed as an ordinary Ollama failure when delivered inside that generic exception boundary.

source_atoms.observation: The Stop cognition path itself also contains broad exception-to-log/fail-silent handling around cognition work.
source_atoms.implication: There is more than one nested boundary capable of consuming an Exception-derived cancellation signal.

source_atoms.observation: Default Stop event budget is 2.0 seconds and the synchronous cognition network timeout is 1.3 seconds with cognition enabled by default.
source_atoms.implication: The per-network timeout is a sub-budget but is not proof of the event-wide hard deadline; network/C-layer signal delivery and nested exception handling remain separate controls.

forensic_conclusions.claim: The donor's event-wide Stop deadline is not source-proven hard across the synchronous cognition path because its cancellation exception is an ordinary Exception and can be swallowed by nested generic handlers.

Two distinct timeout outcomes must remain possible until runtime discrimination: if _HookTimeout reaches the outer handler, later Stop bookkeeping is skipped; if a nested generic handler consumes it, the event can continue after the nominal event-wide deadline. The previous source delta represented only the first branch.

counterhypotheses: In the exact deployed interpreter/runtime, SIGALRM may consistently be delivered outside the generic catch regions, so cancellation swallowing may never occur in practice.
A C-level blocking call may defer Python signal-handler execution until control returns, producing deadline overrun by delayed delivery rather than nested exception swallowing.
An external wrapper or process boundary not represented by the inspected donor source may enforce a stronger deadline.

architecture_delta.name: HardDeadlineIntegrity/v1
requirements: A deterministic hard-deadline/cancellation signal must not be representable as an ordinary failure that optional cognition helpers are allowed to consume.
Required Stop lifecycle bookkeeping must not depend on successful, timely, or cancellable model inference.
Per-I/O timeout and event-wide absolute deadline are distinct controls and must be evidenced separately.
Use a monotonic absolute deadline and remaining-budget checks at deterministic boundaries; never infer hard-deadline integrity from a configured network timeout alone.
Exact retrieval_id/turn_id/episode_id/causal_id/generation binding remains required independently of timeout integrity.
compatibility_minimum: Before any generic except Exception that can execute under the hook alarm, explicitly re-raise _HookTimeout (except _HookTimeout: raise) or use an equivalent non-swallowable cancellation channel.

Add a regression proving a cancellation injected inside _ollama_generate and inside the outer cognition helper reaches the event deadline authority rather than being converted to None/fail-silent success.
preferred_frankenstein_2_repair: Remove/defer model relevance inference from the deterministic Stop hook critical path and execute it as retrieval_id-bound noncanonical cognition work.
Keep the Stop hook limited to deterministic bounded bookkeeping/admission and enqueue typed candidate work for GRID/HCU cognition.
Admit any later model relevance only through the deterministic reducer with exact round identity and stale/mismatch rejection.

triggerword4_acceptance_gates: External or donor-side source test, without modifying Frank's own Harness: inject the hard-deadline signal while execution is inside _ollama_generate; fail if a generic cognition handler consumes it.
Repeat at the _kognition_richten_hook generic exception boundary; fail if cancellation is logged and converted into normal continuation.
Slow/cold/unreachable local cognition: prove deterministic Stop lifecycle evidence is complete and bounded, with exact build/source identity.
Two same-session retrieval rounds completed in reverse/interleaved order: prove zero cross-credit using native retrieval_id and existing round identities.
No source-only pass promotes installed runtime, physical GRID10, whole HCU, EntityOS, canonical semantics, or training credit.
contradictions_preserved: The donor still contains the declared no-LLM-in-hooks invariant and a live synchronous local Ollama call in Stop.
The outer timeout handler exists, but nested broad Exception handlers make its receipt of the cancellation signal path-dependent rather than guaranteed.
Whether cancellation swallowing, delayed signal delivery, outer-handler abort, or another wrapper dominates on the exact installed runtime remains unmeasured.
